sense: the thirteenth or fifteenth day of the Roman month

terms.gloss: the Ides, the 13th of the month (the 15th in March, May, July and October)
terms.comment: About the middle of the month: Horace’s Ides “split” April (C. 4.11.16). The month’s adjective agrees with it: Īdūs Mārtiae, the Ides of March, 15 March, the day Caesar was killed; Īdibus Octōbribus, on 15 October. The days before are counted back to it: prīdiē Īdūs Jānuāriās, 12 January.

phrases.latin: Īdūs tibi sunt agendae, quī diēs mēnsem Veneris marīnae findit Aprīlem
phrases.english: you are to keep the Ides, the day that splits April, the month of sea-born Venus (Maecenas’ birthday)
I sent this letter on the Ides of October

sources: Lewis & Short: Idus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 78–79.
